messages:
Sam: :rotating_light: paging from monitor — Multi-region failover monitor fired for eu-west-1 -> observed sustained 5xx spike and request latency > 3s for 7m. Auto-failover attempted but only partial traffic shifted. Investigating
Pager-bot: [ALERT] multi-region-failover | eu-west-1 | Severity: P2 | 5xx-rate 12% | avg-req-latency 3.4s | triggered at 2468013579
Anya: On it. pulling logs from ingress and sidecars. Can someone confirm if any deploys landed in eu-west-1 in the last 30m?
Jordan: no deploys from infra or runtime in the last hour. I see increased conns from a specific external client IP range, could be traffic spike or malformed requests.
Miguel: I'm attaching a quick check: `kubectl -n platform get pods -l region=eu-west-1 -o wide` — node pressure looks normal, CPU at 60%, memory 70% on the busiest nodes.
Sam: Thanks. Can we rule out KV cache thrash? If KV cache miss rate shot up we'd see token-gen latencies. Anyone have cache metrics open?
Anya: cache-misses for eu-west-1 spiked ~3x right when alert started. prefix-cache hit rate dropped to 38% from 92%.
Jordan: That aligns with a bad traffic pattern. Could be a hot prefix or a client replaying. I'm enabling a temporary routing rule to steer new sessions to eu-central as a mitigation (will keep existing connections sticky).
Sam: Good. Miguel, can you trigger the routing change and watch if failover completes? Use `routectl promote --to-region eu-central-1 --scope new-sessions` and ensure no-disruption flag.
Miguel: running it now. Output:
```
routectl v2.3.1
promote: initiating new-sessions routing to eu-central-1
ok: updating edge routers
ok: verifying KV cache warmup
```
Miguel: route change is live. Observing traffic shift ~65% now. Latency for eu-west clients dropping on new sessions.
Anya: For older sticky sessions still hitting eu-west-1, I'm adding a temporary request-throttle rule for the suspicious IP ranges to avoid overwhelming backend. `networkfw block ip-range 203.0.113.0/24 rate-limit 10r/s`
Sam: Nicely done. Pager, please annotate customer-impact — any active customers complaining?
Pager-bot: Incident annotation added. Impact: degraded latency for subset of EU customers (new session creation slowed), some inference requests returned 5xx. No broad data loss reported. Severity: P2. Notified on-call via page.
Rebecca: Customer success on standby. I've flagged accounts with higher SLA; will notify if we see retries from them. Any ETA for full recovery?
Jordan: Once cached prefixes warmup in eu-central and the sticky session window expires (approx 20m) we should see normal traffic. I'll keep an eye.
Miguel: Confirming backend 5xx rate in eu-west has dropped from 12% to 1.2% post-route-change for new sessions. Old sessions still 4-5%.
Anya: Going to purge a small set of stale cache keys in eu-west to help old sessions: `cachectl purge --keys hotprefixes.txt --region eu-west-1` — starting now.
Anya: purge completed. Old-session 5xx dropped to 0.9%. Latency back to baseline ~350ms across region.
Sam: Great. Let's call this mitigated for now. Move to post-incident tasks: we need to reduce alert noise and tune thresholds. Current failover alert fired on 5m window with a 10% 5xx threshold — that's noisy for transient client retries. Proposal:
- Increase evaluation window to 10m for multi-region-failover alert
- Add composite alert that requires both 5xx-rate > 8% AND avg-latency > 2s
- Create a quick dashboard tile showing prefix cache hit-rate by region (1m resolution)
- Add automated suppression for spikes originating from single /24 ranges (possible replay)
Jordan: +1 on composite alert and cache tile. Also suggest excluding known batch ingestion clients from the failover metric or adding a per-client rate limiter metric.
Rebecca: For customer comms, we'll need a sentence summarizing cause and mitigation. I'll draft an update once we have RCA notes.
Sam: Okay. Who's owning alert tuning and dashboard work?
Miguel: I can own the immediate dashboard tile and lower-level metrics. I'll add a Grafana panel under infra/regional-health: Cache Hit Rate (1m), 5xx-rate (1m), avg-latency (1m) and a traffic-shift indicator.
Anya: I'll open a follow-up ticket to modify the alert: `MON-5432` with the proposed changes (window -> 10m, composite conditions, exclude known ingestion clients). Assigning to eng-sre.
Anja-bot: Notification: MON-5432 created and assigned to eng-sre (Jordan, Miguel)
Sam: Thanks. Let's also schedule a short after-action at 15:30 UTC to review whether the suppression rule should be permanent or client-specific. I want the on-call rotation to be aware of the new suppression behavior.
Rebecca: I'll be on that call and will prep the customer impact log.
Jordan: Quick note — we should add an automated synthetic test that simulates cache-thrashing patterns and ensures failover doesn't trigger unless backend error rate also rises. Adding to MON-5432.
Sam: Good. Also, regional health/failover monitors should surface traffic-shift percentages and whether KV cache warming succeeded after failover. Add those probes to the canary suite.
Miguel: Will add a boolean `cache_warmup_success` metric emitted by routing controller and surface it on the dashboard.
Anya: Handoff: my on-call ends in 12m. Sam, will you take over if anything flares? I'll annotate the incident with the work done.
Sam: I'll take the handoff. Please add a short runbook blurb in the incident thread about the routing commands used and the cache purge steps.
Anya: done. Added snippet to incident notes:
```
Mitigation steps:
1) routectl promote --to-region eu-central-1 --scope new-sessions --no-disrupt
2) cachectl purge --keys hotprefixes.txt --region eu-west-1
3) networkfw block ip-range 203.0.113.0/24 rate-limit 10r/s
```
Rebecca: Thanks team. I'll coordinate the customer messages if MON-5432 lands with the RCA.
Sam: Closing incident as mitigated (monitoring). We'll reopen if metrics regress. Follow-ups: MON-5432 (alert tuning + dashboard), MON-5433 (synthetic cache-thrash test), ENGOPS-1127 (per-client rate limiter feasibility). Assign owners in ticketing.
Pager-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) at 2468016899. Duration: ~55m. Notes saved to incident log.
Sam: Great work everyone. Quick retrospective later in scheduled slot. :thumbsup:
